title: Authentication and Authorization: From First Principles to Tokens

contract.reader: A developer or reviewer of web applications and HTTP APIs who uses sessions, OAuth 2.0 or JSON Web Tokens through a framework and wants the model behind them
contract.problem: Passwords, cookies, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect and JWTs look unrelated, and common defects (ID tokens accepted at APIs, decoding instead of validating, missing object-level checks) come from confusing what each answers
contract.outcome: Separate identification, authentication, authorization and audit; compare reference and value tokens; explain what OAuth 2.0 delegates and what OpenID Connect adds; validate a JWT access token in order; enforce object-level authorization; state how long each credential outlives a sign-out
contract.contribution: A top-down path from the reference monitor to current IETF practice (RFC 9068, RFC 9700) in which each protocol appears after the problem it solves, with an ordered validation procedure, pseudocode and a threats-and-controls table; the series' map and its only treatment of token validation and lifecycle
contract.evidence: 23 references, mostly the IETF RFCs themselves, plus OpenID Connect Core 1.0, XACML 3.0, OWASP API Security Top 10 2023, Anderson (1972), Saltzer and Schroeder (1975)
contract.limitations: Overview depth for authenticators, sessions, authorization models, grants, sender-constrained tokens and service-to-service calls (entries 2 to 7); no framework or vendor; the cookie revision is cited as an Internet-Draft

findings.location: Sections 1.2, 5.4, 7.2 and 9, the four Mermaid diagrams (all viewports)
findings.problem: No caption and no accessible name (facts.json: 4 SVG figures without title)
findings.whyItMatters: Captions should say what to notice (standards 6.8); screen readers announce unnamed graphics for the page's clearest statement of the PKCE and refresh flows
findings.action: Add accTitle/accDescr to each diagram and a one-sentence caption (Figure component or site-level caption syntax)
findings.acceptance: facts.json reports 0 SVG figures without title and each diagram has a caption

findings.problem: Message labels wrapped narrowly and crossed by lifelines; 'grant_type=refresh_tok-en' hyphenated inside the parameter name; at 360 px text about 7 px and the Resource server column off-screen
findings.whyItMatters: A broken parameter name is a detail readers copy; on a phone the flows need zooming
findings.action: Site level: wider sequence spacing and label backgrounds in the Mermaid config; article: shorten the longest labels
findings.acceptance: At 1280 px no label is crossed by a lifeline and no parameter name is hyphenated; at 360 px labels legible without zoom or figure visibly scrolls

findings.location: Section 1.2 flowchart (mobile-light-07) and Section 9 pipeline (mobile-light-55), 360 px
findings.problem: Right part of each flowchart hidden without a cue: the Audit log node; the successful branch (Business logic, Response)
findings.whyItMatters: In Section 9 the hidden branch is the path the pipeline leads to
findings.action: Site-level scroll cue for wide figures (as DFT and FFT L2), or a top-to-bottom layout for the Section 9 pipeline
findings.acceptance: At 360 px every node is visible or a visible cue shows that the figure scrolls

findings.problem: 'two parties hold copies, one of which must be an attacker' overstates: a legitimate client retrying after a lost response also presents a rotated token; RFC 9700 4.14.2 says only that the server cannot tell which party
findings.whyItMatters: Implementers who believe reuse proves an attack are surprised by spurious sign-outs
findings.action: Say reuse means the token may have been copied and the server, unable to tell an attacker from a retrying client, revokes the chain; optionally mention a grace period
findings.acceptance: The Rotation item no longer says one holder must be an attacker and names the benign case

findings.problem: No links to entries 4 (Authorization Models), 5 (OAuth 2.0 Grants and Client Types) and 7 (Service-to-Service Authentication), although these sections summarize them; entries 2, 3 and 6 are linked
findings.whyItMatters: A reader needing depth on one layer has no pointer at the point of need in a 33-minute article (standards 8.1)
findings.action: One linked sentence at the end of Sections 2.2, 4.2 and 5.4 naming the entry that goes deeper
findings.acceptance: Sections 2.2, 4.2 and 5.4 each link the corresponding later entry on the live page
